title: Fast Power (x^n)
description: Implement `myPow(x, n)`, which calculates `x` raised to the integer power `n` (`x^n`) using binary exponentiation. Note that `n` can be zero or negative, including `-2^31`, and answers are compared within a floating-point tolerance of `1e-5`.
hints: Promote `n` to a 64-bit signed integer before negating it so `-2^31` does not overflow; when `n < 0`, replace `x` with `1.0 / x` and negate `n`.
Repeatedly square `x` and shift `n` right by 1 bit, multiplying into the result whenever the lowest bit of `n` is 1.
